design_rationale: The study explicitly used a computer-generated randomization list prepared by a statistician, with allocation concealed from the recruitment coordinator until randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and concealed, and reported baseline characteristics were broadly balanced, but coordinator errors affected allocation for eight participants and create concern about implementation of the randomization process.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was completed via a computer-generated randomization list issued by a statistician with block sizes of 10 and concealed from the recruitment coordinator until randomization... Six participants were incorrectly randomized to the intervention and two to the control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and caregivers could not be blinded, adherence to regular treatment declined, and substantial control-group emollient use reduced separation between conditions; although described as intention-to-treat, the complete-case analysis and analysis by the coordinator's ultimate assignment leave some concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 2, 6 and 12 months, the intervention group had 87%, 72.4% and 66.7% high adherence, respectively, vs. 45.2%, 45.8% and 45.5% in the control group... The primary clinical end point analysis was conducted on an intent-to-treat basis using a complete case approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome data were missing for 28% of randomized participants, substantially exceeding the anticipated attrition, and the primary complete-case analysis provided no convincing evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcome or balanced in its causes across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Lost to follow-up was 28.0% for the primary end point... The primary clinical end point analysis was conducted on an intent-to-treat basis using a complete case approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome used established diagnostic criteria, was assessed consistently, and was diagnosed by an investigator blinded to assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of AD at 12 months diagnosed by a blinded investigator... The criteria for the development of AD were the U.K. Working Party Criteria adapted to identify incident cases of AD.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and a post hoc alternative definition of AD was added because of dropout, creating potential for selective reporting among outcome definitions and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because of the large dropout rate, a post hoc secondary analysis of the primary outcome was also performed using the cumulative incidence of AD diagnosed by any of the following – a blinded investigator, non-investigator physician or provider-diagnosed AD recorded in the medical record.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven chiefly by 28% missing primary-outcome data handled with a complete-case analysis without evidence that missingness was noninformative. Additional concerns arise from randomization implementation errors, imperfect adherence and contamination, and an unregistered/post hoc analytic option.

paper_title: d6fc477a_Br J Dermatol - 2017 - Lowe - A randomized trial of a barrier lipid replacement strategy for the prevention of atopic
design_rationale: The report explicitly describes a randomized, parallel controlled trial and acknowledges assistance with developing the randomization sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: A randomization sequence was developed and baseline factors were generally balanced, but the sequence-generation method and allocation-concealment procedure are not reported in the available text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We thank Dr Lyle Gurrin, University of Melbourne, for assistance with developing the randomization sequence

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial used intention-to-treat analysis and adherence was fairly high, but parents were necessarily aware of treatment and substantial non-protocol emollient use, particularly in controls, could have diluted the intervention contrast.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Use of other emollients (not study treatment) for on average ≥ 3 days per week during the intervention period occurred in 39% of the control group and 18% of the intervention group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for nearly all randomized infants through 12 months, with denominators generally between 34 and 39 per group out of approximately 40 randomized per group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There was minimal loss to follow-up at each time point (Appendix S1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Clinical outcomes were evaluated by a blinded assessor, standardized AD definitions and skin-testing procedures were used, and measurement appears comparable between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical follow-up of infants by a blinded assessor (C.A.) occurred at 6 weeks, 6 months and 12 months of age.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistered protocol or prespecified analysis plan is described in the available report, while multiple outcome definitions, time points, and intention-to-treat, adjusted, and per-protocol analyses were available, creating scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Per protocol analyses (only including infants who received ≥ 5 days per week of study treatment) revealed a significant reduction in food sensitization at 12 months in the treatment group

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment, differential use of nonstudy emollients in an unblinded behavioral intervention, and lack of clear prespecification amid multiple outcomes and analyses. Missing outcome data were minimal and outcome assessment was blinded and standardized.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized, parallel-group trial using a computer-generated pseudo-random sequence and secure internet-based allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer generated with variable permuted blocks, concealed through a secure centralized internet system, and baseline characteristics were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomisation schedule was created by the CTU using computer-generated pseudo-random code with permuted blocks of randomly varying size. The sequence was known only to the programmer until database lock.

domain_judgments.rationale: Families were unmasked, adherence declined over time and some control families used emollients, although the primary analysis appropriately retained participants as randomized regardless of adherence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participating families were not masked... satisfactory adherence was 88% (466 of 532) at 3 months, 82% (427 of 519) at 6 months, and 74% (375 of 506) at 12 months... contamination occurred in 18% (82 of 457) at 3 months, 17% (62 of 372) at 6 months, and 15% (49 of 324) at 12 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome data were available for about 87% of randomized infants with similar retention between groups, and multiple-imputation and other missing-data sensitivity analyses agreed with the primary result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At age 2 years, eczema was present in 139 (23%) of 598 infants with outcome data collected in the emollient group and 150 (25%) of 612 infants in the control group... Sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary analysis, by use of data from GP records for missing primary outcome data, imputed missing data, and CACE analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome used validated diagnostic criteria applied consistently by trained, masked research nurses; only 3% of follow-up assessments were accidentally unmasked, and a fully masked visible-eczema assessment corroborated the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was diagnosis of eczema over the past year (defined by the UK working party refinement of the Hanifin and Rajka diagnostic criteria for eczema) assessed by research nurses masked to treatment allocation at age 2 years... Accidental unmasking of outcome assessors to treatment allocation occurred for 3% of families at the 2-year visits.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the primary outcome and two-year analysis were preplanned, and a statistical analysis plan was finalized before database lock, making selective reporting unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysis and publication of data for the 2-year primary outcome timepoint were preplanned... Further details are presented in the appendix and SAP, finalised before the database lock... The trial was registered at the ISRCTN registry before initiation of recruitment, ISRCTN21528841.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by unmasked families, declining intervention adherence, and some contamination in controls. Randomization and concealment were robust, outcome assessment was largely masked, missing-data analyses were reassuring, and prospective registration and prespecification reduced reporting-bias concerns.

design_rationale: This was a cluster-randomized 2×2 factorial trial using a computer-generated allocation scheme based on geographical living-area and 3-month time blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The computer-generated cluster allocation was explicitly random and baseline characteristics were generally similar, but concealment of the geographically and temporally blocked sequence until cluster assignment was not clearly described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To reduce the risk of intervention contamination across the groups within locally organised wellbaby maternity groups, we used computer-generated cluster randomisation based on 92 geographical living area blocks as well as eight 3-month time blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were unmasked and adherence was low, with a small amount of contamination and erroneous intervention delivery, although the primary analysis followed intention-to-treat and sensitivity analyses were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Another limitation of our study was the low full protocol adherence of 27% in the skin emollient group and 32% in the early complementary feeding group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome missingness was appreciable and differential across groups (4–14%), and the primary best-case imputation materially differed from complete-case and multiple-imputation estimates, indicating that results could be biased by missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data for the primary endpoint were missing in 24 (4%) of 596 infants in the no intervention group, 76 (13%) of 575 in the skin intervention group, 45 (7%) of 642 in the food intervention group, and 79 (14%) of 583 in the combined intervention group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Atopic dermatitis was measured using recognized diagnostic criteria at scheduled visits, consistently across groups, by investigators masked to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Atopic dermatitis by age 12 months was the primary outcome, based on clinical investigations at 3, 6 and 12 months by investigators masked to group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome and main analysis were prespecified in a registered protocol and statistical analysis plan before unmasking, while post-hoc analyses were clearly labeled.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was prespecified in the protocol, while the sensitivity analyses were specified in the SAP prior to any analyses and unmasking of the randomisation.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because differential missing outcome data reached 13–14% in intervention groups and conclusions were sensitive to the method used to handle missingness. There were also some concerns about allocation concealment and substantial nonadherence in this unmasked behavioral trial, despite masked outcome assessment and prespecified analyses.

design_rationale: The infants were explicitly allocated to four intervention groups using computerized random numbers through a central randomization system based on minimization.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computerized random-number system with central allocation and minimization on prespecified prognostic factors was used, and reported baseline characteristics were generally similar across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Babies born at term were randomized into 4 groups according to gender (male or female), mode of delivery (vaginal or Caesarean) and family history of allergic diseases (present or absent) using computerized random numbers. Randomization was performed at a central location.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open to caregivers, adherence was imperfect, control families could use emollients, and the analysis excluded randomized infants with unavailable post-randomization data rather than clearly following intention-to-treat, creating potential intervention contamination and deviation-related bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The control group was not prevented from applying emollients due to ethical reasons.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for only 459 of 549 randomized infants (83.6%), with exclusions made when data were unavailable after randomization and no evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcomes or balanced by group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 459 babies from the 4 groups completed the intervention and qualified for assessment of the primary outcome at 1 year of age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome depended substantially on caregiver questionnaires in an unblinded, non-treatment-controlled trial, so caregiver knowledge of assignment could influence reporting, despite blinded confirmation being described for a separate 9-month clinical assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: AD was diagnosed according to the criteria of the Japanese Dermatological Association [12], when an itchy rash lasting 2 or more months was reported in the questionnaires returned at 1, 6, and 9 months and 1 year of the baby’s age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and a primary outcome and analysis were specified, but the report presents multiple AD definitions and comparisons, and the registered protocol or prespecified analysis plan is not supplied to verify that the reported operationalizations and analyses were selected without flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In addition, AD was diagnosed using the U. K. Working Party’s Diagnostic Criteria included in the questionnaire at 1 year.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because substantial post-randomization missing outcome data were excluded, the control group could use the skin-care intervention and analyses were not clearly intention-to-treat, and the caregiver-reported primary outcome was susceptible to knowledge of assignment. Central computerized randomization was a strength, but it does not offset these high-risk domains.

paper_title: b0154209_The Journal of Dermatology - 2017 - Yonezawa - Effects of moisturizing skincare on skin barrier function and the prevention
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports individual central randomization using stratified blocks of size two or four with a 1:1 allocation ratio.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central, stratified block randomization likely concealed allocation, but the sequence-generation method is not fully described and there were statistically significant baseline imbalances in outcome-relevant skin measures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed individually according to central registration after measuring the skin barrier function at baseline. The randomization sequence used two or four blocks and was stratified according to whether the newborns were term and weighed more than 2500 g.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded, both groups were explicitly allowed to depart from assigned care, substantial moisturizer use occurred in controls, and the modified intention-to-treat analysis excluded randomized participants, although observed exposure differences remained clear.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the intervention group, if parents were resistant to reducing the frequency of bathing, they were allowed to bathe their newborn daily, but they could only use soap every other day. In the control group, parents were allowed to apply a moisturizer to their newborns if they wanted to.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for 202/227 randomized infants (89.0%), with somewhat greater loss in the intervention group, and no analysis established that missingness could not bias the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, we analyzed the data of 202 infants (89.0%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although instrumental skin-barrier outcomes used standardized methods, measurement personnel were unblinded and secondary skin problems were recorded by unblinded parents using partly original criteria, making intervention-aware outcome assessment plausibly differential.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Second, we could not blind the measurer or avoid bias among the parents who evaluated the infants’ skin problems.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and identifies a primary outcome, but the supplied report does not establish prospective registration of all detailed measurements and analyses, while numerous anatomical sites, outcome components, derived dry-skin outcomes, time periods, and analyses create scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was registered in the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000013260).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because outcome assessors and parent reporters were unblinded, creating substantial risk of differential measurement, particularly for parent-reported skin problems. Additional concerns arise from incompletely described sequence generation, baseline imbalances, permitted crossover/non-adherence, modified intention-to-treat exclusions, missing data, and possible selective reporting.
